contracts.commit_point: chcode/utils/shell/session.py lines 57-78, culminating in subprocess.Popen([self._provider.shell_path, *spawn_args], ...) at lines 71-78; the guard's blocked short-circuit at lines 52-55 returns before the command is assembled or spawned.
contracts.declared_mechanism: check_command(command) in chcode/utils/shell/guard.py, invoked as the first step of ShellSession.execute (session.py line 43) before command assembly and subprocess.Popen. The guard applies command-position rules (bare dangerous words must appear at a segment leader after optional sudo/doas prefixes, with relative-path invocations exempt; systemctl danger-subcommand and init 0|6 forms covered) and context/flag regex rules over the raw command string across bash/powershell/cmd dialects, honoring the _guard_enabled master switch and _disabled_categories. On a match it returns GuardResult(blocked=True, category, pattern_id); execute then short-circuits, returning ShellResult(exit_code=126, stderr=reason) with empty output and never building full_command or spawning the shell.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A command string matching any active dangerous-command rule (categories recursive_delete, force_kill, system_damage, shutdown) is assembled into full_command and reaches the subprocess.Popen spawn of the provider shell — i.e., ShellSession.execute proceeds past the check_command verdict on a match, or the guard is bypassed/disabled so that a matching destructive command is executed instead of being short-circuited with exit code 126.

The /danger slash-command wiring that calls set_guard_enabled/set_category_enabled (guard.py lines 75-106) and the REPL/config persistence path (~/.chat/chagent. via _load_setting/_update_setting) are not in the supplied views, so whether runtime disabling is user-only or reachable through agent flows is unverified.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of a shell command through ShellSession.execute, which builds the provider command and spawns the shell subprocess; the operation is reached by the agent via the LangChain bash tool, which dispatches its agent-supplied command argument into session.execute.
contracts.protected_resource: The host OS shell/process execution environment reached through ShellSession.execute's subprocess spawn (the system shell and the machine state that destructive commands such as raw-disk writes, recursive deletion, forced kills, and shutdown target).
contracts.protection_obligation: Merged from both reviews (phase 1 German / phase 2 English, same obligation): destructive shell commands must not be assembled or executed by ShellSession.execute. check_command must scan the raw command string before any execution and block every match across the four evaluated categories — recursive deletion (rm with -r/-rf/-fr or --recursive, Remove-Item/ri -Recurse, rmdir|rd /s, del|erase /s), forced kills (kill/killall/pkill -9/-KILL/-SIGKILL, taskkill /f or /t, Stop-Process -Force), system damage (mkfs*, format <drive>:, dd of=/dev/ raw-disk writes, > /dev/sd|nvme|hd raw writes, fork bombs), and shutdown/reboot (shutdown, halt, poweroff, reboot, stop-computer, restart-computer, init 0|6, systemctl poweroff/reboot/halt) — honoring the global guard switch and disabled-category set, and returning ShellResult(exit_code=126) without spawning the shell subprocess.
scope_limits: The guard is opt-out by design: the master switch _guard_enabled (default True) and the per-category _disabled_categories set allow any rule to be bypassed; check_command returns GuardResult(blocked=False) when disabled or when the matched category is disabled (guard.py lines 30-36, 275-276, 288, 296-297).

Detection is a string/regex heuristic on the raw command string; only the enumerated bash/powershell/cmd patterns in _match_position and _CONTEXT_RULES are covered, and relative-path invocations of same-named binaries (e.g., ./reboot) are exempt from position-rule matching (guard.py lines 146-159, 281-284).

Blocked commands return ShellResult(exit_code=126) with a localized reason rather than raising; the guard is enforced only at the ShellSession.execute boundary shown, and no additional enforcement layer appears in the supplied views.
The guard scans only the raw command argument passed to ShellSession.execute; effects of other tools (write_file, edit, etc.) are outside this obligation.
Coverage of nested invocation (cmd /c ...) is asserted only for patterns appearing literally in the command string (guard.py lines 3-5).
